column1: Adults and children are frequently confronted with statements about the alarming rate of loss of tropical rainforests.
column2: 成人和儿童经常接触到关于热带雨林破坏速度令人震惊的陈述。

column1: For example, one graphic illustration to which children might readily relate is the estimate that rainforests are being destroyed at a rate equivalent to one thousand football fields every forty minutes – about the duration of a normal classroom period.
column2: 例如，一个孩子容易理解的形象化说明是：热带雨林正以每四十分钟相当于一千个足球场的速度被破坏——这一时间长度大约相当于一节正常课堂的时间。

column1: In the face of the frequent and often vivid media coverage, it is likely that children will have formed ideas about rainforests – what and where they are, why they are important, what endangers them – independent of any formal tuition.
column2: 面对媒体频繁且生动的报道，孩子们很可能在没有接受任何正式教育的情况下，已经形成了关于雨林的观念——包括它们是什么、在哪里、为什么重要，以及哪些因素会威胁它们。

column1: It is also possible that some of these ideas will be mistaken.
column2: 这些想法也可能是错误的。

column1: Many studies have shown that children harbour misconceptions about ‘pure’,curriculum science.
column2: 许多研究表明，孩子们对于‘纯粹’的科学课程存在误解。

column1: These misconceptions do not remain isolated but become incorporated into a multifaceted, but organised, conceptual framework, making it and the component ideas, some of which are erroneous, more robust but also accessible to modification.
column2: 这些误解并非孤立存在，而是被纳入了一个多方面的、但具有组织性的概念框架中。这样一来，这个框架以及其中的各个组成部分虽然有些是错误的，但仍然相当稳固，并且还可以进行进一步的修改。

column1: These ideas may be developed by children absorbing ideas through the popular media.
column2: 这些想法可能是孩子们通过大众媒体吸收形成的。

column1: Sometimes this information may be erroneous.
column2: 有时候这些信息可能是错误的。

column1: It seems schools may not be providing an opportunity for children to re-express their ideas and so have them tested and refined by teachers and their peers.
column2: 似乎学校可能并未为孩子们提供表达想法的机会，使这些想法能够由教师和同伴进行检验与完善。

column1: Despite the extensive coverage in the popular media of the destruction of rainforests, little formal information is available about children’s ideas in this area.
column2: 尽管大众媒体对雨林破坏的报道非常广泛，但关于儿童对此类问题的看法，却几乎没有正式的研究资料可供参考。

column1: The aim of the present study is to start to provide such information, to help teachers design their educational strategies to build upon correct ideas and to displace misconceptions and to plan programmes in environmental studies in their schools.
column2: 本研究的目的是提供此类信息，帮助教师设计有效的教育策略，以纠正学生的错误观念，并规划学校中的环境研究课程。

column1: The study surveys children’s scientific knowledge and attitudes to rainforests.
column2: 这项研究调查了孩子们对雨林的科学认知以及他们对雨林的态度。

column1: Secondary school children were asked to complete a questionnaire containing five open-form questions.
column2: 中学学生被要求完成一份包含五个开放式问题的问卷。

column1: The most frequent responses to the first question were descriptions which are self-evident from the term ‘rainforest’.
column2: 对于第一个问题，最常见的回答都是那些从‘雨林’这个词就可以直接得出的描述。

column1: Some children described them as damp, wet or hot.
column2: 有些孩子描述说，热带雨林是潮湿、湿润或闷热的。

column1: The second question concerned the geographical location of rainforests.
column2: 第二个问题涉及雨林的地理位置。

column1: The commonest responses were continents or countries: Africa(given by 43% of children), South America (30%), Brazil (25%).
column2: 最常见的回答是大陆或国家：非洲（43%）、南美洲（30%）、巴西（25%）。

column1: Some children also gave more general locations, such as being near the Equator.
column2: 一些孩子还给出了更一般的位置，比如靠近赤道。

column1: Responses to question three concerned the importance of rainforests.
column2: 对第三个问题的回应涉及雨林的重要性。

column1: The dominant idea, raised by 64% of the pupils, was that rainforests provide animals with habitats.
column2: 有64%的学生认为，热带雨林为动物提供了栖息地。这是大家普遍认同的观点。

column1: Fewer students responded that rainforests provide plant habitats, and even fewer mentioned the indigenous populations of rainforests.
column2: 只有少数学生认为热带雨林为植物提供了栖息地，而提到热带雨林中居住的土著居民的人则更少。

column1: More girls (70%) than boys (60%) raised the idea of rainforest as animal habitats.
column2: 认为雨林是动物栖息地的女孩比例（70%）高于男孩比例（60%）。

column1: Similarly, but at a lower level, more girls (13%) than boys (5%) said that rainforests provided human habitats.
column2: 同样地，更多女孩（13%）认为热带雨林为人类提供栖息地，而男孩仅为5%。

column1: These observations are generally consistent with our previous studies of pupils’ views about the use and conservation of rainforests, in which girls were shown to be more sympathetic to animals and expressed views which seem to place an intrinsic value on non-human animal life.
column2: 这些观察结果与我们之前关于学生对雨林利用与保护看法的研究一致，其中女孩表现出更强的动物同情心，其观点似乎赋予非人类动物生命以内在价值。

column1: The fourth question concerned the causes of the destruction of rainforests.
column2: 第四个问题涉及雨林破坏的原因。

column1: Perhaps encouragingly, more than half of the pupils (59%) identified that it is human activities which are destroying rainforests, some personalising the responsibility by the use of terms such as ‘we are’.
column2: 令人欣慰的是，超过一半的学生（59%）认为是人类活动在破坏雨林，其中一些人还用‘我们也是’这样的表述将责任个人化。

column1: About 18% of the pupils referred specifically to logging activity.
column2: 约18%的学生提到了伐木活动。

column1: One misconception, expressed by some 10% of the pupils, was that acid rain is responsible for rainforest destruction; a similar proportion said that pollution is destroying rainforests.
column2: 有10%的学生认为酸雨是导致雨林破坏的原因；同样比例的学生也认为污染正在破坏雨林。

column1: Here, children are confusing rainforest destruction with damage to the forests of Western Europe by these factors.
column2: 在这里，孩子们常常将热带雨林的破坏与西欧森林受到的损害相混淆。

column1: While two fifths of the students provided the information that the rainforests provide oxygen, in some cases this response also embraced the misconception that rainforest destruction would reduce atmospheric oxygen, making the atmosphere incompatible with human life on Earth.
column2: 虽然五分之二的学生认为雨林能够产生氧气，但在某些情况下，这些回答还包含了一个误解：他们认为雨林的破坏会导致大气中氧气的减少，从而使大气环境不再适合人类生存。

column1: In answer to the final question about the importance of rainforest conservation, the majority of children simply said that we need rainforests to survive.
column2: 在回答关于保护雨林重要性这一最后一个问题时，大多数孩子表示，我们需要雨林才能生存。

column1: Only a few of the pupils (6%) mentioned that rainforest destruction may contribute to global warming.
column2: 只有少数学生（占6%）提到，雨林的破坏可能会加剧全球变暖。

column1: This is surprising considering the high level of media coverage on this issue.
column2: 考虑到媒体对此问题的报道频率如此之高，这一情况确实令人惊讶。

column1: Some children expressed the idea that the conservation of rainforests is not important.
column2: 一些孩子认为，保护雨林不重要。

column1: The results of this study suggest that certain ideas predominate in the thinking of children about rainforests.
column2: 这项研究的结果表明，在孩子们对雨林的认知中，某些概念占据着主导地位。

column1: Pupils’ responses indicate some misconceptions in basic scientific knowledge of rainforests’ ecosystems such as their ideas about rainforests as habitats for animals, plants and humans and the relationship between climatic change and destruction of rainforests.
column2: 学生的回答表明，他们在关于雨林生态系统的基础知识方面存在一些误解。例如，他们认为雨林是动物、植物和人类的栖息地，同时也不理解气候变化与雨林破坏之间的关系。

column1: Pupils did not volunteer ideas that suggested that they appreciated the complexity of causes of rainforest destruction.
column2: 学生们并没有主动提出任何表明他们理解雨林破坏原因复杂性的观点。

column1: In other words, they gave no indication of an appreciation of either the range of ways in which rainforests are important or the complex social, economic and political factors which drive the activities which are destroying the rainforests.
column2: 换句话说，他们既没有表现出对雨林重要性各种方面的认识，也没有意识到那些推动着破坏雨林行为的复杂社会、经济和政治因素。

column1: One encouragement is that the results of similar studies about other environmental issues suggest that older children seem to acquire the ability to appreciate value and evaluate conflicting views.
column2: 令人欣慰的是，关于其他环境问题的类似研究结果表明，年龄较大的儿童似乎能够学会评价事物的价值，并区分不同的观点。

column1: Environmental education offers an arena in which these skills can be developed, which is essential for these children as future decision –makers.
column2: 环境教育为这些技能的培养提供了平台，这对这些未来决策者的孩子至关重要。
